dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Well, are you here to brave The Chasm by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's never heard of any commission like that...

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, you don't know about the Guild's commissions yet? Sorry, that's my mistake.

dialogues.speaker: Lan
dialogues.text: Well, The Chasm has been closed for a long time now. No one can go in without the Qixing's say-so, not even the Adventurers' Guild.

choices.text: No special pass for you guys?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Well, we wouldn't dream of being a bother to the people at Yujing Terrace. It would be a counterproductive thing to do, messing with pre-established policy like that.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Even Ms. Ganyu, who seems like the most amicable of the bunch, would probably just smile at us and say "why don't you have some tea while you wait here?"

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: And then she'll leave you hanging for most of the day, until you start wondering whether she'd forgotten all about you till she was nearly off from work...

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Hmph, and as we all know, Ms. Ganyu never gets off work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That certainly does sound like a very Ganyu-esque way of refusing.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Either way, this means that Ms. Katheryne isn't going to be giving out any commissions about The Chasm anytime soon. Instead, we've got to find more... convenient people to help us out in private.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Convenient?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Yes, like for example, miners from Huishan Hall, members of the Millelith, staff at the Ministry of Civil Affairs. They can get passes to go in more easily, and...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And... what?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Well... So what I'm saying is, O valiant hero who saved Liyue from the sea monster, yet seems to have nothing to do all day every day, surely you can talk to the Millelith on our behalf?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No idea who you're talking about.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: I'm talking about you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, she was definitely talking about you!

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Don't play dumb. Who do you think I'm talking about, Rex Lapis?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Alright, quit your bragging.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Whatever the case... You have our thanks for your help so far, and we'd like you to consider helping us again.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: It's fine if the timing isn't convenient for you. It's just that... If you do end up passing through The Chasm, please help me look for a fellow named Muning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Muning... Who's that supposed to be?

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: He's a specialist sent to The Chasm by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. We've got some personal matters that need settling. You can ask him about it if you meet him there.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Just pass this message along: "You still owe Lan money for drinks. Don't you forget that." He'll get the picture.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Wait, hold on a moment! There's one more thing. If you take this commission up, just negotiate your payment directly with Muning.

response.speaker: Lan
response.text: Don't ask me why the arrangement is like this... We did this at the Ministry's insistence. Best not to question their decisions and all...

choices.text: I'll keep an eye out on the way in.
I'll have you know that I do some important work, you know.
They don't close one eye with you lot?
